title: After-hours quant playbook docket
content:
Purpose: late-night scratchpad to capture small experiments + hunches about int4 quant + KV caching interactions. Not polished — notes to self, quick commands, and TODOs.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Aggressive quant (per-channel int4 with symmetric clipping) reduces memory by ~2.3x but amplifies attention noise for long-context tokens. KV cache noise seems to increase when we evict mid-rollout. Maybe due to scale mismatch between quantized keys and unquantized queries when using mixed-precision runtime kernels.

Quick experiment snapshot (run at 03:12 local):
- model: rw-1.3b-v2 (fp16 baseline)
- quant: per-channel int4 + range-clip 99.5%
- batch: 8, seq: 1024, streaming KV enabled
- hardware: g5.2xlarge (A10G-like)
- result: median latency 72ms/token (baseline fp16 55ms/token), p95 220ms (baseline 140ms)
- tokens saved: ~56% memory footprint on weights, KV cache reduced by ~40%
- observed: periodic spikes aligned w/ KV eviction events (~every 120s)

Notes / observations:
- Spikes: profiler shows kernel fallback to slower path when sequence grows >768 after several requests; fallback path appears to dequantize keys into scratch buffers.
- Prefetch idea: pre-warm the dequantized KV for a rolling window of top-k queries (cheap approx) before eviction to smooth spikes. Could add flag: runtime.prefetch_kv_deq_window = 128
- Scale mismatch speculation: per-channel scale computed on weight tile boundaries may differ from scales used for activations; check quantization script for "freeze_scale" vs dynamic scale recompute.

Prompt sets I used (tiny dev set):
- tiny-reasoning-16: 16 prompts, short chain-of-thought style, 4 examples per prompt for few-shot
- multi-turn-quick-10: 10 back-and-forths, each ~120 tokens total
- edge-truncs-6: artificially long prefix tokens to stress KV growth

Short checklist (next runs):
- [ ] Re-run with freeze_scale=true and log per-layer scale histograms (INF-1297 attach)
- [ ] Try symmetric vs asymmetric quant for keys only (weights kept int4, activations bfloat16)
- [ ] Add a microbench that simulates sustained burst traffic (200 qps for 3 minutes) and record p95/p99 latency and memory churn
- [ ] Spike detector in console: event when kernel fallback occurs -> trace id + sample input

Ad-hoc commands (local dev):
- python quantize.py --model rw-1.3b-v2 --mode perchannel --bits 4 --clip 99.5 --freeze-scale
- ./run_microbench --host localhost:8080 --qps 200 --seq 1024 --streaming-kv true --tag afterhours011

Open questions / to-discuss with Riley:
- Is it acceptable to prefer slightly higher average latency if p99 volatile spikes are reduced? For dedicated customers we want predictable tails.
- Should we expose per-route quant profiles in console (e.g., prefer_fp16_for_chat, prefer_int4_for_embeddings)?

Random late-night hunch: sliding-window dequant cache keyed by (model, route, last-n-tokens-hash) — keep warm for heavy routes. Might be over-engineering but could smooth those eviction spikes.

Log of small results (append-only):
- 2026-03-27T03:12: median 72ms/token, p95 220ms (int4-perchannel clip99.5)
- 2026-03-27T03:40: symmetric int4 on KV-only -> median 68ms, p95 190ms (promising)

If I wake up later: try smaller clip (99.0) and record sample logits divergence on tiny-reasoning-16. Save run outputs under GH PR linked above.

Endnotes: this is basically a mental scratchpad. Move promising configs to a proper bench doc and create a controlled ablation matrix before tagging for rollout.
